fork-0.text: These come from real games. The other side moves first, then you answer. Only the strongest move counts. If it goes on, they reply and you keep going. Then I show the whole line of moves, and why it works.
Sometimes you're Black. The board turns round so your pieces are at the bottom, and the letters and numbers turn with it. I'll say whose move it is.

mateIn1-0.text: Mate in one: a checkmate is there to find, this move. Any checkmate counts. Here it's queen to g7: your king guards her, so the black king can't take her.

hangingPiece-0.text: Free pieces: enemy pieces nothing defends. In real games they hide among the others, so see what defends a piece before you take it.

pin-0.text: A pin freezes a piece: moving it would expose what's behind it. This knight can't move, or its king would be in check. Attack a pinned piece and it can't run.

skewer-0.text: A skewer is a pin turned round: the more valuable piece is in front. Here the king has to step off the line, then the rook takes the queen behind him.

backRankMate-0.text: The back rank is a king's home row. When his own pawns box him in, a rook or queen landing on that row is checkmate, unless something can take or block it.

mateIn2-0.text: Mate in two: your move, their reply, your checkmate. Start with a move that leaves one reply, usually a check. Here: rook to e8, check. Their rook has to take, and your other rook mates.

discoveredAttack-0.text: A discovered attack: one piece moves off a line and uncovers the piece behind it. Move this knight and the rook checks the king, while the knight attacks something else.

discoveredAttack-1.text: En passant, a rare pawn rule: a pawn that steps two squares past an enemy pawn can be taken as if it stepped one, on the very next move only. Here f5 takes e5 by landing on e6.

doubleCheck-0.text: Double check: two pieces check the king at once. You can't take or block both, so the king has to move. If he can't, it's checkmate.

trappedPiece-0.text: A trapped piece has nowhere safe to go. This knight's squares, b6 and c7, are both attacked. Bishop to e4 attacks it, and wherever it runs it can be taken.

deflection-0.text: A deflection drags a defender away. Only the rook on d8 guards the queen. Rook to e8, check: their rook has to take, and your other rook takes the queen.

attraction-0.text: An attraction lures a piece, often the king, onto a bad square, usually by offering something to take. Rook to f8, check: the king has to take, then knight to d7 forks him and the queen.
Castling, a king's move once a game: an unmoved king steps two squares toward an unmoved rook, and the rook hops to his other side. Nothing may stand between them, and never out of or through check.

promotion-0.text: Promotion: a pawn reaching the last rank. You pick what it becomes, nearly always a queen. Clear its way, or win the square it lands on.

mateIn3-0.text: Mate in three: three of your moves, two replies. Here every check leaves one reply: rook to e8, your other rook takes on e8, then the queen takes on e8, checkmate.
